scope: Read-only official metadata/source and existing archived evidence. No gameplay rerun, binary download, binary inspection, engine change, or mutation of tests/controllers.

assertions: Both official release inventories publish the same editor and template byte counts and SHA256 digests used by the existing controller.
Original export validation and all three original mode results bind the same exported DWM.exe hash.
This establishes recorded official-asset and local archive custody, not reproducible engine source-to-binary equivalence.

qualifications: The hosting repository tag is release metadata, not Godot engine source.
The release index names a tag and does not resolve the differing banner/source hashes.
The pinned engine forms the banner suffix from the first nine compile-time GODOT_VERSION_HASH characters.
The pinned tarball builder stores a resolved source revision in synthetic .git/HEAD; the released source tarball was not downloaded or inspected.
Prior failed source-identity lookups are retained without repetition in prior-engine-source-identity-note.md.
Historical build script revisions are the last public changes to these paths before asset publication, not an attestation of the exact build inputs used.

symbols.configuration_inference: Public pre-release Windows configuration selects production=yes and use_mingw=yes without native-symbol overrides for the editor, template_debug and template_release. Pinned SConstruct defaults native symbols off in production and passes -s without symbols. The expected public configuration strips Windows targets; exact tested-EXE symbol absence is not proven.
symbols.debug_template_qualification: template_debug sets DEBUG_ENABLED game-development features, separately from native debug_symbols. A debug target name does not establish retained PDB/DWARF symbols, and its different executable cannot supply exact symbols for the tested release executable.
matching_symbol_prerequisites: Exact original module identity and matching native debug information; PDB GUID/age if using a CodeView/PDB path, or the corresponding matching DWARF/debuglink information for MinGW.
Private AccessKit types/layout or an independently validated decoder for the relevant Rust implementation in the loaded module(s). Godot C++ symbols alone may not decode an opaque Rust adapter.
No matching Windows symbol set for the tested release executable was identified in the inspected official release inventories.

stock_reader.verbose_output: Adapter lifecycle messages, including activation, deactivation and initial-update completion; no emitted edge graph or parent chain.
stock_reader.cli_output: Pinned main.cpp has accessibility mode selection and general verbose/script-debug options; no accessibility-tree dump switch was identified.

dormant_existing_failure_hook.captured: Thread stacks and loaded modules, not a heap/tree snapshot

stock_reader.memory_snapshot_feasibility: No actionable supported exact-symbol graph-decoding route is established from current metadata. A later read-only snapshot could only establish capture-time state if matching symbols/schema and a coherent snapshot are available; it cannot establish the earlier natural in-budget tree update.
boundaries: No standard binary was executed with help, debug, verbose or a tree-dump flag in this audit.
No breakpoints, injection, recompilation or symbols downloaded.
A live noninvasive read is not guaranteed to provide an atomic graph; inconsistent private pointers/edges would be inconclusive.
UIA client projection is not the private AccessKit graph and does not supply a Godot RID mapping.

recommendation: Retain stronger official-asset provenance and the unresolved exact-source qualification. Do not dispatch another stock logging or debug-template run as an emitted-parent-chain discriminator. A future original-binary private-memory plan first needs demonstrably matching symbol/schema availability and a bounded capture protocol; those prerequisites are not supplied by this audit.
